persons.name: Helen W. Henderson
persons.notes: Byline recovered from MS-AR-00017-A, where a line break had merged it into the headline.

persons.name: Ivan Karp
persons.notes: Self-describes in MS-VI-00001 as employed at a fine arts gallery. Also credited with the article in MS-AR-00040 (Barone Gallery, 1960) as "Ivan C Karp".

persons.name: John Dobkin
persons.notes: Speaks in MS-VI-00002 with authority on the National Academy of Design. Note: the transcript opens by recalling Sievan "back in the 20s", which does not fit the expected biography - speaker attribution of that passage needs review.

persons.name: John Ruskin
persons.notes: Byline on a 1979 clipping (MS-AR-00041-A). Not the Victorian critic, who died in 1900 - a pseudonym, a namesake, or a manifest error. Unverified.

persons.name: Joseph Solman
persons.notes: Self-describes in MS-VI-00003: "first recognized in the mid-30s ... for my street scenes"; refers to his studio circle including Rothko and Gottlieb.

persons.name: Joseph Wolins
persons.notes: Self-describes in MS-VI-00004 as exhibiting alongside Sievan at Contemporary Arts Gallery and working with him on the WPA federal art project.

persons.name: Maurice Sievan
persons.notes: The subject of this archive. "Maurice Seivan" is a misspelling in MS-AR-00036.

persons.name: Sam Fienstien
persons.notes: Spelled "Sam Fienstien" in the manifest (MS-AR-00048-C); probably the critic Sam Feinstein. Spelling retained as written pending confirmation.

persons.name: Will Barnet
persons.notes: Discusses Sievan's development as a peer in MS-VI-00005; no explicit self-description of role in the transcript.

places.name: New York City
places.notes: Where Sievan lived and where all but three of the archive's documented exhibitions were held.

places.name: Woodstock, New York
places.notes: The place these sheets name most often, and the only one they name in all three roles at once: painted there, titled after it, and shown there at Kay's in 1970.

places.name: Croton-on-Hudson, New York
places.notes: Sievan writes it lower-case and once with a question mark, on MS-AR-00068, where he was labelling his own sketches from memory.

places.name: Flushing, Queens, New York
places.notes: MS-AR-00070 dates a painting "circa 1946 - 47 in Flushing", which is the archive's only evidence for where Sievan was working in those years.

places.name: Southampton, New York
places.notes: The archive's transcription read "SOUTHHAMPTON" until the sheet was checked against the scan; MS-AR-00053 has one H.

places.name: New Hampshire
places.notes: Two of the eight works on MS-AR-00054 are titled after it, but the sheet says nothing about when he was there.

places.name: Monhegan Island, Maine
places.notes: A painters' colony off the Maine coast. Two works are titled after it, on two different sheets.

places.name: Provincetown, Massachusetts
places.notes: Sievan spells it three different ways across these sheets. The retrospective catalogue records that he shared a Provincetown studio with Mark Rothko.

places.name: Paris
places.notes: Named on MS-AR-00055 only, in brackets, beside "The Chess Game".

places.name: Kay's, Woodstock
places.notes: Where Sievan showed the six 1970 pastels itemised on MS-AR-00075. The archive holds no catalogue, poster or notice for this showing — the sheet is the only record of it.

places.name: Passedoit Gallery
places.notes: The archive documents two Passedoit exhibitions from their own printed matter, and MS-AR-00069 independently records a painting at a Passedoit summer show.

places.name: Contemporary Arts
places.notes: Two documented exhibitions, 1939 and 1941. The venue-matching heuristic deliberately finds no press for them because "Contemporary Arts" is too generic a token to match safely — but Sievan's own sheet MS-AR-00068 names it, which the heuristic could never have done.

places.name: St. Lawrence University, Canton, New York
places.notes: Sievan shipped a painting here on 21 April 1970 for the Dorothy Feigin Memorial Exhibition, "Aranged by the Federation (for Permanent Colection)". His note gives a courier or contact as "Buds Budsworth".

places.name: Art Students League of New York
Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts
places.notes: Named on MS-AR-00064. The retrospective CV does not list it, so this is the archive's only evidence that a Sievan hung there.

places.name: North Shore Art Festival, Great Neck
places.notes: MS-AR-00066 gives the address as 100 Cutter Mill Road.

attestedWorks.quote: WOODSTOCK LANDSCAPE 12 x 16
STUDIO INTERIOR 12 x 16

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with the price and the buyer below
attestedWorks.quote: "SOUTHAMPTON LANDSCAPE 18 x 24 oil on canvas board" Bottom center: "350" with a ghost mark for "450" from an erasure nearby. Bottom Right: Signed in pen, "Sievan" below "sold to ORR"
attestedWorks.notes: The sheet carries an erased "450" beneath the "350", so the asking price was revised down. The retrospective catalogue's CV lists an "I. David Orr" among the private collections, which is a lead toward identifying ORR, not an identification.

attestedWorks.quote: "1) New Hampshire Landscape" below sketch "water color 9x12 large ebony frame $60"
attestedWorks.notes: The numbers 1-8 on this sheet are Sievan's own, running across both faces.

attestedWorks.quote: "2) Pines (all over) $150 16 x 12"
"3) Croton On the Hudson $125 12x16"
4) Near the East River 16 x 20 oil 300 (200 marked over)
attestedWorks.notes: The price was written over an earlier figure, so 300 supersedes 200.

attestedWorks.quote: "5) IN NEW HAMPSHIRE" below sketch "water color 10 x 14 $75"
"6) oil 12x16 $125 LANDSCAPE"
attestedWorks.notes: "LANDSCAPE" alone is how Sievan labelled several unrelated works; it should not be read as a distinguishing title.

attestedWorks.quote: "7) gouache 16x20 winter landscape $250"
attestedWorks.notes: Written lower-case, so whether "winter landscape" is a title or a description is not recorded.

attestedWorks.quote: 8) Flushing Landscape water color large one unframed 13 1/2 x 20 $100
attestedWorks.notes: The verso also carries a boxed note reading "AT ETHELS". Which of the works on this face it refers to is not recorded, so it is not attached to any of them here.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top left, with the size and place at top right
attestedWorks.quote: "The Chess Game" Top right: 10 3/4 x 12 water color [Paris] Center bottom: 200
attestedWorks.notes: The retired folder MS-AR-00076 was labelled "Drawings of Paintings - Landscape & 1 Chess Players", which is most likely this sheet.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top and right edge, with the title at the foot
attestedWorks.quote: "I have that one back - but (arrow to text block on the right) Right: Running vertically "Rudolph asked to bring this one back to Rudolphs well framed new modern frame ^[wide] [canvas insert] etc like his frames)" Bottom: "ProvenceTown Landscape 25 x 30 on board 400"
attestedWorks.notes: Sievan spells Provincetown three different ways across these sheets; this sheet has "ProvenceTown".

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with the size and the name below
attestedWorks.quote: "Birchland #1" Bottom: "20 x 24 quoted 350: Bottom left: "Irving Cohn"
attestedWorks.notes: The verso reads "Irving Cohn wants this" — an offer, not a sale. Cohn's name appears again on MS-AR-00060 beside a different painting, so he was being offered more than one.

attestedWorks.quote: circled "118" "ALONG THE HIGHWAY" circled "R" (WOODSTOCK NY) by Maurice Sievan 16 x 20 - OIL - 1953 $1,000. (price in graphite) OIL ON CANVAS BOARD ST. LAWRENCE UNIVERSITY (following in graphite) on Apr 21 1970 (Buds Budsworth) FEIGIN MEMORIAL EXHIBITION
attestedWorks.notes: The most fully documented work on any of these sheets, and the only one the archive can corroborate from a second source: the retrospective catalogue's CV lists "St. Lawrence Univ., Canton, NY" among the museum collections. The sheet adds that it went on 21 April 1970, for the Dorothy Feigin Memorial Exhibition, "Aranged by the Federation (for Permanent Colection)". Neither source has been checked against the university's own records.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with the title at the foot
attestedWorks.quote: Oil on paper 15 1/2 x 18 Bottom: SCENE IN WOODSTOCK Bottom Right: 300
EARLY SPRING 22 x 28 oil on canvas board Bottom left: (circled) "Irving Cohn" Bottom center: 450
attestedWorks.notes: The verso repeats "Irving Cohn wants this Quoted 450", and the signature carries an added "+ Ethel & Co" in graphite.

attestedWorks.quote: at Dusk 9 x 12 oil

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with the title at the foot
attestedWorks.quote: For the Art Students League (Oct 1957) 18 x 24 on Canvas board (oil) Bottom: INTERIOR (PROVINCETOWN)
attestedWorks.notes: "For the Art Students League" states an intention. Whether the painting was actually shown there is not recorded.

attestedWorks.quote: variation on a theme (mona liza) 24 x 36
attestedWorks.notes: The only figure subject named anywhere on these sheets; everything else is landscape or interior. Sievan's spelling of Mona Lisa is his own.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Bottom, with a note along the right edge
attestedWorks.quote: "Seascape $500 25 x30" Right edge running vertically: "one was in Pennsylvania Academy As ProvinceTown Seascape"
attestedWorks.notes: "one was in Pennsylvania Academy" implies more than one version, and does not say that this is the one that hung there. The Academy appears nowhere in the retrospective CV, so this sheet is the archive's only evidence for it.

attestedWorks.quote: SPRING HAT 20 x 24
Lower Manhattan 22 28
attestedWorks.notes: The size is written without a separator, so whether it reads 22 x 28 is the transcription's inference and not the sheet's.

attestedWorks.quote: Winter 16 x 20
22 x 28 landscape (on canvas board)
attestedWorks.notes: No title: the sheet records only a size, a medium and the word "landscape".

attestedWorks.quote: "Hampton Bays Landscape 25 x 30 $800" Bottom Right: "Siesta 32 x 40  $800" Right running veritcally: At North Shore Art Festival 100 Cutter Mill Road, Great Neck, NY
attestedWorks.notes: The festival note runs vertically along the edge of the whole sheet rather than beside either painting, so it may cover both works on this face, or only one. The archive does not decide which.

attestedWorks.quote: "Siesta 32 x 40  $800" Right running veritcally: At North Shore Art Festival 100 Cutter Mill Road, Great Neck, NY
attestedWorks.notes: At 32 x 40 the largest work named anywhere on these sheets. The same caveat about the festival note applies as on the sheet's other painting.

attestedWorks.quote: BIRCHLAND BII BIRCHL
attestedWorks.notes: The verso is a trailing-off inscription — "BIRCHLAND BII BIRCHL" followed by scribbles — so even the title is uncertain. MS-AR-00057 records a "Birchland #1". Whether these are two works, one work, or a series is not recorded, and the archive does not merge them.

attestedWorks.quote: (underlined) "Kassner" (below) he has 5 of my paintings" "1 Monhegan Nightscape 20 x 24 oil on canvas" running vertically to the right: "this one is Out" below "I have it back"
attestedWorks.notes: The sheet says Kassner "has 5 of my paintings" and then lists six. This is the one marked "this one is Out" and "I have it back", so it is most likely the one that came back — but that is the archive's reading of the arithmetic, not something the sheet states. MS-AR-00071 names the same dealer, which is how the spelling was settled.

attestedWorks.quote: "2 Suburbia #4 28 x 24 on canvas board"
attestedWorks.notes: The consignment is stated once at the head of the sheet — "Agreement is that I get $300 for each he'll sell each for $450" — not beside this line. A "#4" in the title implies at least four Suburbia paintings; the archive knows of no others.

attestedWorks.quote: "3) THE POOL 350 20 x 24 on canvas board"
attestedWorks.notes: The consignment is stated at the head of page 1, not beside this line.

attestedWorks.quote: "4) Landscape #12 20 x 24 oil on canvas"
attestedWorks.notes: Numbered "#12" in Sievan's own landscape series, of which the archive can name only this one and "Landscape #3" on MS-AR-00074 and "Landscape #13" on MS-AR-00075. The consignment is stated at the head of page 1.

attestedWorks.quote: "5) In my Naborhood 20 x 24 oil on canvas board"
attestedWorks.notes: Sievan's spelling. The consignment is stated at the head of page 1.

attestedWorks.quote: "6) Sag Harbor 20 x 24 oil on canvas"
attestedWorks.notes: The consignment is stated at the head of page 1.

attestedWorks.quote: "9 x 12 OIL at Contemporary"
attestedWorks.notes: Written at the head of the sheet, above a column of seven sketches, so it may be a heading for the whole sheet or a note about one painting. The verso repeats it and adds "sold" and "and two water colors", which matches the note beside the first sketch — so this may be the same work as the entry below and not a separate one. The archive does not decide.

attestedWorks.quote: #1 "Painted with Mac" "Near the River" (green pencil) "O + 2 water colors"
attestedWorks.notes: "Painted with Mac" is the only note on these sheets that records Sievan painting in company. Who Mac was is not recorded.

attestedWorks.quote: #2 "croton" (arrow in red pencil) "Sold to Collectors"
attestedWorks.notes: No title — "croton" is a place label in the sheet's left-hand column, not a title. Whether "Collectors" is a gallery name or simply the plural noun is not recorded.

attestedWorks.quote: #3 "croton?" "a grey day" "Sold collectors"
attestedWorks.notes: Sievan's own question mark after "croton" is the reason this place link is marked uncertain — he was labelling his sketches from memory and was not sure. Written lower-case, so whether "a grey day" is a title or a description of the weather is not recorded. MS-AR-00070 records a "Gray Day" in ink with an inventory number; whether that is this painting is not recorded, and the archive does not merge them.

attestedWorks.quote: #4 no note, "Suburban landscape" (green pencil) "only this one at Franc(?) yet still left on this paper
attestedWorks.notes: The transcriber could not read the name after "at", and neither can the archive; it is left as the sheet has it.

attestedWorks.quote: #5 "Church at Ver Planck at miss Marsh (red pencil) over ->
attestedWorks.notes: The scan shows SOLD in red pencil across this entry.

attestedWorks.quote: #6 "croton same mildred Painted"
attestedWorks.notes: No title. Who Mildred was, and whether she painted alongside him or bought the picture, is not recorded. The scan shows SOLD in red pencil beneath this entry.

attestedWorks.quote: #7 bottom, image right turned vertically "downtown 12 x 16 OIL (in green pencil) O Back"
attestedWorks.notes: Written lower-case. "Back" is read here as the painting having come back to him, which is how the same word is used on MS-AR-00070 and MS-AR-00067.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with a note along the right edge
attestedWorks.quote: "MORNING LANDSCAPE $250, oil on canvas board 12 x 16 painted (1955) Right running vertically: "at Passedoit Summer show"
attestedWorks.notes: The archive separately documents two Passedoit exhibitions, in 1955 and 1957, from the gallery's own printed matter. This sheet is independent evidence of a Passedoit summer show and of one painting in it.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with the title and date below
attestedWorks.quote: "I got this back (underlined) from Orr (He revarnished it)" Bottom: in ink "Gray Day" #180 (circled) "oil on Academy board 18 x 24" in graphite "$400 canvas" in ink "circa 1946 - 47 in Flushing.
attestedWorks.notes: The only work on these sheets whose place of making is stated rather than implied by the title. Orr also appears on MS-AR-00053, where a painting is "sold to ORR" — so the same collector both bought a Sievan and returned another. The retrospective CV lists "I. David Orr" among the private collections.

attestedWorks.quote: "(at sundown) took them Apr 6 1958 16x20
attestedWorks.notes: "took them" is plural, so the date records a day on which several paintings were collected, not necessarily the day this one was made.

attestedWorks.quote: "small interim" "16 x 20? 400"
attestedWorks.notes: Sievan's own question mark after the size: he was unsure of it himself. The verso also carries the fragment "Kassner" and "2 20 x 24 =", which is the second sheet to name that dealer.

attestedWorks.quote: "Brooklyn Bridge 16 x 20 oil Manhattan Landscape $65
attestedWorks.notes: The line carries two names, "Brooklyn Bridge" and "Manhattan Landscape". Which is the title and which is the subject is not recorded.

attestedWorks.quote: "Monhegan Seascape 16 x 20 oil $65"
attestedWorks.notes: The cheapest works named anywhere on these sheets. At $65 against the $800 asked on MS-AR-00066, this sheet is probably much the earlier of the two, though neither is dated.

attestedWorks.quote: "12 x 16 oil Croton Landscape $50"
attestedWorks.notes: The lowest price recorded on any of these sheets. This sheet is a fragment of an envelope.

attestedWorks.quote: sold to Jenns Friends daughter. 22 x 28 oil The Highway
attestedWorks.notes: The buyer is recorded only by her relation to someone else, which is as far as the evidence goes. MS-AR-00058 records a different painting titled "ALONG THE HIGHWAY"; the archive keeps them apart.

attestedWorks.sheet_position: Top, with notes right and below
attestedWorks.quote: circled "12" "Landscape #3 16 x 20" Right: "approx $150" Bottom: "Zitners House, small one) oil framed (in red pencil) I think she sold this one for $100"
attestedWorks.notes: "I think she sold this one for $100" is Sievan uncertain about his own painting's sale, so price_usd is left empty and only his words are kept. The retrospective CV lists a "Charles Zitner" among the private collections. Two different numbers appear here: a circled 12 and the title's own #3.

attestedWorks.quote: 925 "WINDOWSCAPE" by MAURICE SIEVAN 10 x 12 1/2 PASTEL 1970, copies watercolors 8 1/2 x 11
attestedWorks.notes: The showing is recorded once at the foot of the sheet — "Shown at Kay's 1970 in Woodstock" — and covers the numbered pastels above it. Sievan also noted a watercolour copy of this work at 8 1/2 x 11. The head of this sheet carries his instruction to himself: "measure Hight first".

attestedWorks.quote: 926 "Along RIVERSIDE DRIVE by M.S. 6 3/4 x 13 1970 51/4 x 11 W.C.
attestedWorks.notes: The medium is not written on this line; it is taken from the group of 1970 pastels this sheet itemises, and from the watercolour copy noted beside it. The showing is recorded at the foot of the sheet.

attestedWorks.quote: 929 Marker "I Kept this one" Ink "by M.S. "Beautiful Landscape" 10 x 12 1/2 - Pastel 1970 81/2 x 11 W.C.
attestedWorks.notes: Circled on the sheet in blue: "I Kept this one". The one work on these sheets that Sievan records keeping, which makes it the likeliest of these to have reached the estate.

attestedWorks.quote: 928 by MS "LANDSCAPE" 11 x 13 1/2 PASTEL 1970 8 1/2 x 11 W.C." Bottom: Shown at Kay's 1970 in Woodstock
attestedWorks.notes: The price is the sheet's group figure for the Kay's pastels, written on the verso as "at Kays 1-2-3-4 pastels only $300 each", not a price for this work alone.

attestedWorks.quote: 205 "Landscape" #13 by MAURICE SIEVAN 18 x 24 - OIL on academy board $700 net.
attestedWorks.notes: Deliberately NOT linked to Kay's: the verso says "at Kays 1-2-3-4 pastels only", and this is an oil with an inventory number from a different range. The most expensive work named on these sheets.

attestedWorks.quote: 927 LANDSCAPE #2 by MAURICE SIEVAN 10 x 12 1/2 pastel 1970 at Kays.
attestedWorks.notes: The only one of the six whose line names Kay's directly rather than relying on the note at the foot of the recto.
